pluss::timeindex::print¶

Back to TimeIndex Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

std::string pluss::timeindex::print(
    const pluss::TimeIndex& index,
    const pluss::TimelinePrintOptions& options = {})

std::ostream& pluss::timeindex::print(
    std::ostream& stream,
    const pluss::TimeIndex& index,
    const pluss::TimelinePrintOptions& options = {})

Render One Structural Representation¶

print() produces human-readable diagnostic text for the TimeIndex as a whole. It labels the object as TimeIndex, reports its one-dimensional shape and timezone when requested, and formats visible instants through the same calendar engine used by Timeline.

The string overload returns the complete representation. The stream overload writes directly to an existing stream and returns that same stream for chaining. Neither overload modifies the index. Stream insertion (stream << index) is the concise default-format equivalent; use print when layout or timestamp formatting must be controlled.

This is presentation, not serialization. The default format shows whole seconds and truncation can insert an ellipsis. Use host() when exact epoch nanoseconds are the data being exchanged.

Layout Options¶

Field

Meaning

Default

format

Calendar format used for each visible instant

%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S

edge_items

Values retained at each side of a truncated axis

3

max_cols

Largest one-dimensional axis shown without truncation

7

show_header

Include the TimeIndex(...) header

true

show_shape

Include shape in the header

true

show_tz

Include timezone in the header

true

max_rows and max_slices are members of the shared option type but do not affect rank-one TimeIndex output.

Examples¶

Example 1. Obtain the default representation as a string.

auto index = pluss::timeindex::make({
    "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2025-01-02T00:00:00Z",
    "2025-01-03T00:00:00Z", "2025-01-04T00:00:00Z",
    "2025-01-05T00:00:00Z"});
std::cout << pluss::timeindex::print(index) << "\n";

Output¶

TimeIndex(shape=[5], tz=UTC)
[ 2025-01-01 00:00:00, 2025-01-02 00:00:00, 2025-01-03 00:00:00, 2025-01-04 00:00:00, 2025-01-05 00:00:00 ]

Example 2. Bound a long axis, show only dates, and omit timezone metadata.

pluss::TimelinePrintOptions options;
options.format = "%F";
options.max_cols = 3;
options.edge_items = 1;
options.show_tz = false;
std::cout << pluss::timeindex::print(index, options) << "\n";

Output¶

TimeIndex(shape=[5])
[ 2025-01-01, ..., 2025-01-05 ]

Example 3. Write directly to a stream and verify stream identity.

std::ostringstream buffer;
auto& returned = pluss::timeindex::print(buffer, index, options);
std::cout << std::boolalpha << (&returned == &buffer) << "\n";
std::cout << buffer.str() << "\n";

Output¶

true
TimeIndex(shape=[5])
[ 2025-01-01, ..., 2025-01-05 ]

Example 4. Remove the structural header for embedding into another report.

options.show_header = false;
std::cout << pluss::timeindex::print(index, options) << "\n";

Output¶

[ 2025-01-01, ..., 2025-01-05 ]

Cost¶

Formatting currently visits every lane before layout truncation, so runtime is O(index.size()) even when only edge values appear. The string overload owns its returned allocation. The stream overload avoids that final returned string but still allocates formatted lane text internally.
